diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $W \in W^{2,\infty}(\Omega)$, then $\K$ is Hilbert-Schmidt, hence compact, on $L^2(\Omega)$.

Furthermore, there exist (generalized) eigenfunctions $\{\varphi_n\}$ of $\Hcal$ and $\{\varphi_n^*\}$ of $\Hcal^*$ such that $\langle \varphi_n,\varphi_m^*\rangle = \delta_{nm}$, and the linear spans of $\{\varphi_n\}$ and $\{\varphi_n^*\}$ are both dense in $L^2(\Omega)$.
Combining Lemmas~\ref{lem:perturb-pure} and ~\ref{lem:K-bounded} concludes the result.

issues.failure_explanation: The argument establishes at most compact resolvent after adding K. The source proves K compact but not self-adjoint or otherwise spectrally symmetric. A compact bounded non-self-adjoint perturbation of a self-adjoint compact-resolvent operator may have complex eigenvalues, and compact resolvent alone does not guarantee completeness of all root vectors or a biorthogonal eigenbasis.

failure_location.quote: Its spectrum consists of isolated real eigenvalues of finite multiplicity accumulating only at $\pm\infty$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove an additional self-adjointness or similarity/completeness structure for K and H, or substantially weaken the proposition to compact resolvent and discrete possibly complex spectrum.
issues.overall_effect: The assertions of real spectrum and dense biorthogonal generalized eigenfunction systems are unsupported, undermining the advertised spectral description of the full linearization.
issues.title: Compact non-self-adjoint perturbation does not imply real complete spectrum
issues.why_classification: The available argument only supports a materially weaker spectral theorem, while recovering reality and completeness would require new operator structure not supplied in the source.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\mathcal L \coloneqq \A + \D_W$ is the linearized operator around $\bar\mu$.

issues.failure_explanation: Mass conservation gives P L=L, hence invariance of the zero-mean range, but not L P=L. From the displayed definitions, L barμ generally equals W(barμ), rather than zero, so subtracting the barμ component before applying L can change the result. Thus commutation is stronger than, and does not follow from, mass conservation.

failure_location.quote: Since $\Pcal$ commutes with $\Lcal$ (mass conservation), it follows that $\Pcal_H$ commutes with $\Hcal$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the commutation claim by the one-sided invariance P L=L and formulate H0 explicitly as the restriction of H to the invariant zero-mean transformed subspace.
issues.overall_effect: The stated justification for commutation and the reduced Schrödinger construction is false, although range invariance is sufficient for defining the restriction actually needed later.
issues.title: The zero-mean projector need not commute with the linearization
issues.why_classification: A short local reformulation using the already available mass-conservation identity preserves the reduced dynamics.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By \autoref{lem:spectrum_finite}, the spectrum of $\Lcal$ in the half-plane $\Re\lambda\ge -\delta$ consists of exactly $m < \infty$ eigenvalues $\{\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m\}$.

Let $(\lambda_i, \phi_i)$ for $i=1,\dots,m$ be the eigenpairs of $\Lcal^*$, chosen so that  
    \[
    \langle\psi_j,\phi_i\rangle_{L^2_{\bar\mu^{-1}}}=\delta_{ij}.
    \]

issues.failure_explanation: Finiteness does not imply that the m listed eigenpairs exhaust the half-plane; the theorem only says those first m satisfy the inequality. In addition, the proof assumes a delta-biorthogonal pairing between right and adjoint eigenvectors. For a defective eigenvalue this can fail—for a Jordan block, its right and left eigenvectors can be orthogonal—so choosing B_j=ψ_j need not pass the Hautus test. The source explicitly allows generalized eigenfunctions and supplies no semisimplicity hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: Assume the first $m$ eigenpairs $\{(\lambda_j,\psi_j)\}_{j=1}^m$ of $\Lcal$ satisfy $\Re\lambda_j \ge -\delta$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, enumerate the entire unstable spectral subspace with multiplicities and construct controls that are nondegenerate on every adjoint eigenspace, treating Jordan chains and real controls for complex modes.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed δ-stabilizability is not established, and consequently the Riccati stabilizing feedback and nonlinear local exponential stabilization are not guaranteed in the stated generality.
issues.title: The Hautus design omits unstable modes and defective eigenspaces
issues.why_classification: Repair requires a new finite-dimensional spectral controllability construction or restrictive semisimplicity assumptions, and the central feedback guarantee otherwise fails.
